title.raw: 卷37 列傳第29 寇儁 韓褒 趙肅 張軌 李彥 郭彥 裴文舉 高賓 Volume 37 Biographies 29: Kuo Jun; Han Bao; Zhao Su; Zhang Gui; Li Yan; Guo Yan; Pei Wenju; Gao Bin

sentences.zh: 寇儁 韓褒 趙肅 張軌 李彥 郭彥 裴文舉 高賓

translations.literal: Kou Jun, Han Bao, Zhao Su, Zhang Gui, Li Yan, Guo Yan, Pei Wenju, Gao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jun; Han Bao; Zhao Su; Zhang Gui; Li Yan; Guo Yan; Pei Wenju; and Gao Bin.

sentences.zh: 寇儁字祖俊，上谷昌平人也。

translations.literal: Kou Jun, styled Zujun, was a man of Changping in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jun, courtesy name Zujun, came from Changping in Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 祖贊，魏南雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zan was Wei Southern Yong Provincial Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zan had served Wei as inspector of Southern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 父臻，安遠將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen held the ranks of general who pacifies the distance and inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 儁性寬雅，幼有識量，好學強記。

translations.literal: Jun by nature was broad and refined; from youth he had discernment and capacity; he loved learning and had a strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was generous and cultivated by temperament. Even as a boy he showed judgment and breadth of mind, loved study, and remembered whatever he read.

sentences.zh: 兄祖訓、祖禮及儁，竝有志行。

translations.literal: His elder brothers Zuxun and Zuli together with Jun all had will and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers Zuxun and Zuli, like Jun himself, were men of purpose and integrity.

sentences.zh: 閨門雍睦，白首同居。

translations.literal: Within the inner gates harmony prevailed; they lived together until white-haired age.
translations.idiomatic: The household was harmonious, and the brothers kept one home together into old age.

sentences.zh: 父亡雖久，而猶於平生所處堂宇，備設帷帳几杖，以時節列拜，垂涕陳薦，若宗廟焉。

translations.literal: Though their father had long been dead, they still in the hall and rooms where he had lived in life fully set out curtains, tables, and staffs; at the proper seasons they lined up to bow, shed tears, and set out offerings, as though at an ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Long after their father's death they still kept his rooms furnished with curtains, tables, and walking sticks, and at each season they bowed there in order, weeping as they laid out offerings, as if before a family shrine.

sentences.zh: 吉凶之事，必先啟告，遠行往返，亦如之。

translations.literal: For matters of fortune or misfortune they always first reported to him; on departing on a distant journey or returning, they did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Whether good or ill befell the family, they told him of it first; the same held when anyone set out on a long journey or came home again.

sentences.zh: 性又廉恕，不以財利為心。

translations.literal: His nature was also incorrupt and forgiving; he did not take wealth and profit to heart.
translations.idiomatic: He was likewise upright and forbearing and never let gain govern his actions.

sentences.zh: 家人曾賣物與人，而剩得絹五匹。

translations.literal: A member of the household once sold something to someone and afterward had five bolts of silk left over.
translations.idiomatic: Once a servant sold goods for the family and came away with five bolts of silk still in hand.

sentences.zh: 儁於後知之，乃曰：「惡木之陰，不可暫息；

translations.literal: Jun afterward learned of it and thereupon said: "The shade of an evil tree — one may not rest there even briefly;
translations.idiomatic: When Jun learned of it later he said, "One should not even pause in the shadow of a wicked tree;

sentences.zh: 盜泉之水，無容誤飲。

translations.literal: The waters of Stolen Spring — one may not drink them by mistake.
translations.idiomatic: nor drink by accident from Stolen Spring.

sentences.zh: 得財失行，吾所不取。

translations.literal: To gain wealth and lose conduct — that I do not accept.
translations.idiomatic: To keep money won at the cost of one's character is something I will not do.

sentences.zh: 」遂訪主還之。

translations.literal: " He then sought out the owner and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: " He tracked down the buyer and gave the silk back.

sentences.zh: 其雅志如此。

translations.literal: His refined purpose was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the fineness of his principles.

sentences.zh: 以選為魏孝文帝挽郎，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: Through selection he became a pallbearer for Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, and was appointed attendant at court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen for imperial service, he served as a pallbearer at Emperor Xiaowen's funeral and was then made attendant at court audiences.

sentences.zh: 大乘賊起，燕齊擾亂，儁參護軍事東討，以功授員外散騎侍郎，遷尚書左民郎中。

translations.literal: When the Mahayana rebels rose and Yan and Qi were thrown into turmoil, Jun took part in military affairs on the eastern campaign; for merit he was given acting attendant of scattered cavalry and transferred to left-section director in the Masters of Writing for the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mahayana rebels erupted and Yan and Qi fell into chaos, Jun joined the staff of the eastern punitive force; for his service he received acting attendant of scattered cavalry and was moved to left-section director in the Masters of Writing for the people.

sentences.zh: 以母憂不拜。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his mother he did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post while mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 正光三年，拜輕

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengguang, he was appointed General of Light
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang year 3 he was made general of light

translations.literal: (Cavalry) [emended: Chariot]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Chariot]

sentences.zh: 〔車〕將軍，遷揚烈將軍、司空府功曹參軍，轉主簿。

translations.literal: 〔Chariot〕 General; he was transferred to General Who Inspires Awe, staff officer of the Ministry of Works, and then chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: chariots, promoted to general who inspires awe and staff officer under the Ministry of Works, and then made chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時靈太后臨朝，減食祿官十分之一，造永寧佛寺，令儁典之。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Dowager Ling held court; she cut the salaries of officeholders by one tenth and built Yongning Buddhist Temple, ordering Jun to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Dowager Ling ruled from behind the screen she trimmed official salaries by a tenth and built Yongning Buddhist Temple, putting Jun in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 資費巨萬，主吏不能欺隱。

translations.literal: The funds ran to tens of thousands; the chief clerks could not conceal anything from him.
translations.idiomatic: Costs ran into the tens of thousands, yet no clerk could hide a thing from him.

sentences.zh: 寺成，又極壯麗。

translations.literal: When the temple was completed, it was also extremely grand and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple stood finished, it was magnificently imposing as well.

sentences.zh: 靈太后嘉之，除左軍將軍。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling commended him and appointed him General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling praised his work and made him general of the left army.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，朝議以國用不足，乃置鹽池都將，秩比上郡。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era the court debated that state expenses were insufficient; they therefore established the post of salt-pond commandant, rank equal to an upper commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang period, with treasury funds running short, the court created the post of salt-pond commandant, ranked equal to an upper commandery.

sentences.zh: 前後居職者，多有侵隱。

translations.literal: Those who had held the post before and after mostly embezzled and concealed revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Previous holders of the office had often skimmed and concealed receipts.

sentences.zh: 乃以儁為之。

translations.literal: Jun was therefore made to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was therefore appointed to the post.

sentences.zh: 加龍驤將軍，仍主簿。

translations.literal: He was given the added rank General of Soaring Dragon and still served as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was also promoted to general of soaring dragon while continuing as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 永安初，華州民史底與司徒楊椿訟田。

translations.literal: At the opening of Yongan, the people of Hua Province, Shi Di, sued Minister of Works Yang Chun over fields.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongan era, a commoner of Hua Province named Shi Di brought a land suit against Minister of Works Yang Chun.

sentences.zh: 長史以下，以椿勢貴，皆言椿直，欲以田給椿。

translations.literal: The chief administrator and those below, because Chun's power and rank were lofty, all said Chun was in the right and wished to give the fields to Chun.
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator and his subordinates, awed by Chun's influence, all declared for him and wanted the land turned over to him.

sentences.zh: 儁曰：「史底窮民，楊公橫奪其地。

translations.literal: Jun said: "Shi Di is a poor commoner; Lord Yang forcibly seized his land.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Shi Di is a destitute farmer, and Lord Yang has seized his land by force.

sentences.zh: 若欲損不足以給有餘，見使雷同，未敢聞命。

translations.literal: If you wish to harm the insufficient to supply the surplus, you make me echo the same word — I dare not accept the order.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to strip the needy to enrich the powerful, you ask me only to parrot the rest — I cannot obey.

sentences.zh: 」遂以地還史底。

translations.literal: " He thereupon returned the land to Shi Di.
translations.idiomatic: " He then restored the fields to Shi Di.

sentences.zh: 孝莊帝后知之，嘉儁守正不撓，卽拜司馬，賜帛百匹。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaozhuang afterward learned of it and commended Jun for holding to rectitude without bending; she at once appointed him marshal and granted a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiaozhuang heard of it she praised Jun for standing firm on principle and immediately made him marshal, granting him a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其附椿者，咸譴責焉。

translations.literal: Those who had sided with Chun were all reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: All who had backed Chun were censured.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為左將軍、

translations.literal: In the second year he went out as Left General and
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was sent out as left general and

translations.literal: (Cool) [emended: Liang]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Liang]

sentences.zh: 〔梁〕州刺史。

translations.literal: 〔Liang〕 Provincial Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: provincial inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 民俗荒獷，多為盜賊。

translations.literal: The customs of the people were wild and fierce; many became bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom was rough and violent, and banditry was widespread.

sentences.zh: 儁乃令郡縣立庠序，勸其耕桑，敦以禮讓，數年之中，風俗頓革。

translations.literal: Jun then ordered the commanderies and counties to establish schools, encouraged them in plowing and mulberry culture, and instructed them in ritual and yielding; within several years the customs were suddenly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had commanderies and counties open schools, urged farming and sericulture, and taught courtesy and forbearance; within a few years the region's ways changed entirely.

sentences.zh: 梁遣其將曹琰之鎮魏興，繼日版築。

translations.literal: Liang sent its general Cao Yanzhi to garrison Weixing, building ramparts day after day.
translations.idiomatic: Liang posted its general Cao Yanzhi at Weixing, raising fortifications day by day.

sentences.zh: 琰之屢擾疆埸，邊人患之。

translations.literal: Yanzhi repeatedly harassed the border; the frontier people were troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi raided the frontier again and again, and border folk lived in dread of him.

sentences.zh: 儁遣長史杜休道率兵攻克其城，幷擒琰之。

translations.literal: Jun sent Chief Administrator Du Xiudao to lead troops, storm and take his city, and also capture Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun dispatched Chief Administrator Du Xiudao at the head of an army, seized the city, and took Yanzhi prisoner.

sentences.zh: 琰之卽梁大將軍景宗之季弟也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was the youngest brother of Liang's great general Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was the youngest brother of the Liang commander Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 於是梁人憚焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the men of Liang feared him.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Liang forces feared him.

sentences.zh: 屬魏室多故，州又僻遠，梁人知無外援，遂遣大兵頓魏興，志圖攻取。

translations.literal: Just then the Wei house had many troubles, and the province was also remote; the men of Liang knew there was no outside aid, and therefore sent a great army to encamp at Weixing, intending to attack and seize it.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei beset by troubles and the province far from help, Liang learned that no relief would come and massed a large force at Weixing, set on capturing the province.

sentences.zh: 儁撫勵將士，人思效命。

translations.literal: Jun comforted and encouraged officers and soldiers; the men thought to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Jun rallied and heartened his officers and men until every soldier was ready to die for him.

sentences.zh: 梁人知其得衆心也，弗之敢逼。

translations.literal: The men of Liang knew he had won the hearts of the multitude; they did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he commanded the loyalty of his troops, the Liang army did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 儁在州清苦，不治產業。

translations.literal: While Jun was in the province he lived in plain austerity and did not manage estates.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his tenure he lived plainly and acquired no property.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，其子等竝徒步而還。

translations.literal: When his term ended, his sons and the rest all returned on foot.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, he and his sons walked home without carriage or escort.

sentences.zh: 吏人送儁，留連於道，久之乃得出界。

translations.literal: Officials and people escorted Jun and lingered on the road; only after a long while did he finally leave the border.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials and commoners followed him along the road and would not let him go; he was a long time crossing the frontier.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，東魏授儁洛州刺史，儁因此乃謀歸闕。

translations.literal: In Datong year 2, Eastern Wei appointed Jun Inspector of Luo Province; Jun therefore planned to return to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong, Eastern Wei named him inspector of Luo Province, and he used the appointment as cover to plan his defection to the Zhou court.

sentences.zh: 五年，將家及親屬四百餘口入關，拜秘書監。

translations.literal: In year 5 he brought his household and more than four hundred kin through the passes and was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he led his family and more than four hundred relatives into Guanzhong and was made director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時軍國草創，墳典散逸，儁始選置令史，抄集經籍，四部羣書，稍得周備。

translations.literal: At the time the army and state were newly founded and the classics and statutes were scattered and lost; Jun first selected and placed clerks, copied and gathered canonical texts, and the books of the four categories gradually became complete.
translations.idiomatic: With the dynasty still young and libraries in disarray, Jun first appointed record clerks to copy and collect the classics until the four divisions of the library were once again in good order.

sentences.zh: 加鎮東將軍，封西安縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: He was given the added rank General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed Baron of Xi'an county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was also promoted to general who pacifies the east and enfeoffed as baron of Xi'an with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十七年，除車騎大將軍、儀同三司，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Three Departments, and given the added post Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments, with the added title regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 儁以年老乞骸骨，太祖弗許。

translations.literal: Jun, because of old age, begged to retire; the Grand Progenitor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked leave to retire on account of age, but Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai refused.

sentences.zh: 遂稱疾篤，不復朝覲。

translations.literal: He thereupon claimed grave illness and no longer attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded serious illness and stopped appearing at court.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年，賜姓若口引氏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was granted the surname Ruokouyin clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei he received the clan name Ruokouyin.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵為子，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, his rank was advanced to viscount and his fief increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he was raised to viscount and given five hundred additional fief households.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，增邑幷前二千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng he was advanced to Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Opening-Office Equal in Three Departments, and his fief together with the former totaled two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 1 he was promoted to grand general of fast cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments, and his fief, old and new together, reached two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 儁年齒雖邁，而志識未衰，教授子孫，必先禮典。

translations.literal: Though Jun's years and teeth had advanced, his will and knowledge had not declined; in instructing sons and grandsons he always began with the ritual classics.
translations.idiomatic: Though well into old age, his mind remained sharp; when he taught his descendants he always started with the rites.

sentences.zh: 世宗尚儒重道，特欽賞之，數加恩錫，思與相見。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong honored Confucian learning and valued the Way; he especially admired him, repeatedly added favor and gifts, and wished to meet with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, who prized learning and the Way, admired him deeply, showered him with honors, and longed to see him in person.

sentences.zh: 儁不得已，乃入朝。

translations.literal: Jun, having no choice, then entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse any longer, Jun came to court.

sentences.zh: 世宗與同席而坐，因顧訪洛陽故事。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong sat on the same mat with him and thereupon turned to inquire about old stories of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shared his seat and questioned him about Luoyang in former days.

sentences.zh: 儁身長八尺，鬚鬢皓然，容止端詳，音韻清朗。

translations.literal: Jun was eight feet tall; his beard and temples were snowy white; his bearing and deportment were dignified and careful; his voice was clear and resonant.
translations.idiomatic: Jun stood eight feet tall, with snow-white beard and temples, a grave and measured bearing, and a voice clear as a bell.

sentences.zh: 帝與之談論，不覺屢為前膝。

translations.literal: The Emperor discussed with him and without noticing repeatedly leaned forward on his knees.
translations.idiomatic: As they talked the emperor kept leaning forward unconsciously, drawn in by every word.

sentences.zh: 及儁辭還，帝親執其手曰：「公年德俱尊，朕所欽尚，乞言之事，所望於公。

translations.literal: When Jun took leave to return, the Emperor personally grasped his hand and said: "Sir, your years and virtue are both honored; you are one I admire and esteem; on matters where I beg your words, it is you I look to.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun prepared to leave, the emperor took his hand and said, "Your age and character command my deepest respect. When I ask counsel, it is you I turn to.

sentences.zh: 宜數相見，以慰虛想。

translations.literal: You should often meet with me, to comfort my empty longing.
translations.idiomatic: Come often, so that my longing to see you may be eased.

sentences.zh: 」以御輿令於帝前乘出。

translations.literal: " He had the imperial carriage ordered before the Emperor for Jun to ride out on.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had the imperial carriage brought up and made Jun ride away in it before the whole court.

sentences.zh: 顧謂左右曰：「如此之事，唯積善者可以致之。

translations.literal: He turned and said to those at his side: "Matters like this — only one who has accumulated goodness can bring them about.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his attendants he said, "Only a lifetime of virtue wins such treatment.

sentences.zh: 何止見重於今，亦將傳之萬古。

translations.literal: How much more than being honored today — it will also be handed down for ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: This is honor not only for today but for all posterity.

sentences.zh: 」時人咸以為榮。

translations.literal: " People of the time all regarded it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: " Contemporaries all counted it the highest distinction.

sentences.zh: 保定三年卒，時年八十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding he died, aged eighty at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Baoding year 3 at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘆惜之，贈本官，加冀定瀛三州諸軍事、冀州刺史，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sighed in regret; posthumously he was granted his former office and given command of military affairs for the three provinces Ji, Ding, and Ying, and Inspector of Ji Province; posthumous title: Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu mourned his loss, confirmed his last offices posthumously, made him commander of armies in Ji, Ding, and Ying and inspector of Ji Province, and gave him the posthumous name Yuan.

sentences.zh: 儁篤於仁義，期功之有孤者，衣食豐約，俱與之同。

translations.literal: Jun was earnest in humaneness and righteousness; for kinsmen within mourning obligation who had orphans, whether food and clothing were abundant or spare, he shared alike with them.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply committed to kindness and duty, he shared whatever he had — feast or famine — with orphaned kin within the circle of mourning obligation.

sentences.zh: 少為司徒崔光所知，光命其子勵與儁結友。

translations.literal: In youth he was known to Minister of Works Cui Guang; Guang ordered his son Li to become friends with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he won the notice of Minister of Works Cui Guang, who told his son Li to befriend him.

sentences.zh: 儁每造光，常清言移日。

translations.literal: Whenever Jun visited Guang, they often conversed in pure talk for whole days.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jun called on Guang they would talk quietly together from morning until night.

sentences.zh: 小宗伯盧辯以儁業行俱崇，待以師友之禮。

translations.literal: Lesser Minister of Rites Lu Bian, because Jun's learning and conduct were both lofty, treated him with the courtesy due a teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Minister of Rites Lu Bian, impressed by Jun's scholarship and character, honored him as both teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 每有閒暇，輒詣儁讌語彌日。

translations.literal: Whenever he had leisure he would go to Jun's and feast and converse for whole days.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had free time he visited Jun and stayed the day in conversation and shared meals.

sentences.zh: 恆謂人曰：「不見西安君，煩憂不遣。

translations.literal: He always said to people: "If I do not see Lord Xi'an, vexation and worry do not depart.
translations.idiomatic: He often told others, "Without a visit to Lord Xi'an, my cares never lift.

sentences.zh: 」其為通人所敬重如此。

translations.literal: " He was respected by the broadly learned in this way.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of learning esteemed him to that degree.

sentences.zh: 子奉，位至儀同三司、大將軍、順陽郡守、洵州刺史、昌國縣公。

translations.literal: His son Feng rose to Opening-Office Equal in Three Departments, Great General, Administrator of Shunyang Commandery, Inspector of Xun Province, and Duke of Changguo county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng rose to opening-office equal in three departments, great general, administrator of Shunyang, inspector of Xun Province, and duke of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 奉弟顒，少好學，最知名。

translations.literal: Feng's younger brother Yong from youth loved learning and was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's younger brother Yong loved study from boyhood and was the best known of the family.

sentences.zh: 居喪哀毀。

translations.literal: While in mourning he was consumed by grief and wasted his body.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his parents he grieved so deeply that his health broke.

sentences.zh: 歷官儀同大將軍，掌朝、布憲、典祀下大夫，小納言，濩澤郡公。

translations.literal: In office he reached Opening-Office Great General, grand masters of court, promulgation of laws, and lower sacrificial rites, lesser director of speech, and Duke of Huoze commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In office he became opening-office great general, grand master of court, grand master for promulgating laws, grand master of lower sacrificial rites, lesser director of speech, and duke of Huoze.

sentences.zh: 韓褒字弘業，其先潁川潁陽人也。

translations.literal: Han Bao, styled Hongye, his ancestors were men of Yingyang in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Bao, courtesy name Hongye, came from a line originally of Yingyang in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 徙居昌黎。

translations.literal: They moved and settled in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: The family later relocated to Changli.

sentences.zh: 祖瑰，魏鎮西將軍、平涼郡守，安定郡公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui was Wei General Who Pacifies the West, Administrator of Pingliang Commandery, and Duke of Anding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui had served Wei as general who pacifies the west, administrator of Pingliang, and duke of Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 父演，征虜將軍、中散大夫、恆州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yan was General Who Campaigns against Barbarians, Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan held the ranks of general who campaigns against barbarians, grand master of palace leisure, and inspector of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 褒少有志尚，好學而不守章句。

translations.literal: Bao from youth had lofty aspiration; he loved learning but did not cling to chapter-and-line reading.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Bao nursed high ambitions; he loved books but refused to be bound by rote commentary.

sentences.zh: 其師怪而問之。

translations.literal: His teacher wondered and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: His teacher was puzzled and asked him why.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「文字之間，常奉訓誘。

translations.literal: He replied: "Between the lines of the text I always receive instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In the words themselves I always find teaching enough.

sentences.zh: 至於商較異同，請從所好。

translations.literal: As for weighing and comparing differences and sameness, please let me follow what I prefer.
translations.idiomatic: When it comes to arguing fine points of agreement and dispute, let me read as inclination leads me.

sentences.zh: 」師因此大奇之。

translations.literal: " The teacher therefore greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " His teacher was astonished and held him in special regard.

sentences.zh: 及長，涉獵經史，深沉有遠略。

translations.literal: When grown, he ranged through the classics and histories; he was deep and reserved and had far-reaching design.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he read widely in the classics and histories, and proved thoughtful, restrained, and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 魏建明中，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Jianming era of Wei he first entered office as attendant at court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Jianming reign he began his career as attendant at court audiences.

sentences.zh: 加彊弩將軍，遷太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was given the added rank General of Strong Crossbows and transferred to Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of strong crossbows and then to grand master of palace counsel.

sentences.zh: 屬魏室喪亂，褒避地於夏州。

translations.literal: Just then the Wei house fell into disorder; Bao sought refuge in Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei court fell into chaos, Bao took refuge in Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 時太祖為刺史，素聞其名，待以客禮。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand Progenitor was provincial inspector; he had long heard of Bao's name and treated him with guest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was then provincial inspector; having long known Bao's reputation, he received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 及賀拔岳為侯莫陳悅所害，諸將遣使迎太祖。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, the generals sent envoys to welcome the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue murdered Heba Yue, the generals sent envoys to summon Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 太祖問以去留之計。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor asked him for counsel on whether to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai asked his advice on whether to remain or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 褒曰：「方今王室淩遲，海內鼎沸。

translations.literal: Bao said: "At present the royal house is in decline; within the four seas it seethes like a boiling cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Bao replied, "The imperial house is failing and the realm boils with unrest.

sentences.zh: 使君天資英武，恩結士心。

translations.literal: My lord, by Heaven's gift you are heroic and martial; your kindness binds the hearts of men of honor.
translations.idiomatic: My lord, Heaven has made you bold in war and generous in spirit, and the gentry are bound to you in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 賀拔公奄及於難，物情危駭。

translations.literal: Lord Heba suddenly met disaster; men's minds are shaken with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Heba has fallen in an instant, and every heart is shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 寇洛自知庸懦，委身而托使君。

translations.literal: Kou Luo knows himself to be mediocre and cowardly; he has entrusted himself to my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo knows his own weakness and has put himself wholly in your hands.

sentences.zh: 若總兵權，據有關中之地，此天授也，何疑乎！

translations.literal: If you gather military authority and hold the land of Guanzhong, this is Heaven's grant — what doubt is there!
translations.idiomatic: If you take command of the armies and hold Guanzhong, that is Heaven's own gift — why hesitate!

sentences.zh: 且侯莫陳悅亂常速禍，乃不乘勝進取平涼，反自遁逃，屯營洛水。

translations.literal: Moreover Houmochen Yue has rebelled against order and rushed toward ruin; he did not seize victory to advance and take Pingliang, but instead fled on his own and encamped on the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: And Houmochen Yue, having turned traitor and courted disaster, failed to press his advantage against Pingliang and instead fled to camp on the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 斯乃井中蛙耳，使君往必擒之。

translations.literal: He is but a frog in a well; if my lord goes you will surely capture him.
translations.idiomatic: He is no more than a frog in a well — if you march against him you will take him at once.

sentences.zh: 不世之勳，在斯一舉。

translations.literal: Unmatched merit rests in this one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: A fame that will last for ages hangs on this single move.

sentences.zh: 時者，難得而易失，誠願使君圖之。

translations.literal: Opportunity is hard to gain and easy to lose; I earnestly wish my lord would plan for it.
translations.idiomatic: The moment is hard to seize and easy to miss; I beg my lord to act on it now.

sentences.zh: 」太祖納焉。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor adopted this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 太祖為丞相，引褒為錄事參軍，賜姓侯呂陵氏。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor became chancellor, he brought in Bao as recording officer on his staff and granted him the clan surname Helbuleng.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai became chancellor, he made Bao recording officer on his staff and granted him the surname Helbuleng.

sentences.zh: 大統初，遷行臺左丞，賜爵三水縣伯。

translations.literal: At the opening of Datong he was transferred to left assistant director of the mobile headquarters and enfeoffed Baron of Sanshui county.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong he was made left assistant director of the mobile headquarters and enfeoffed baron of Sanshui.

sentences.zh: 尋轉丞相府屬，加中軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to staff of the chancellor's office, given the added ranks General of Central Troops and Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the chancellor's staff, promoted to general of central troops and grand master with the silver seal and blue girdle.

sentences.zh: 二年，梁人北寇商洛，東魏復侵樊鄧，於是以褒為鎮南將軍、丞相府從事中郎，出鎮淅酈。

translations.literal: In year 2, Liang forces raided north into Shangluo, and Eastern Wei again invaded Fan and Deng; Bao was therefore made General Who Garrisons the South, consulting staff officer in the chancellor's office, and sent out to garrison Xi and Li.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, when Liang raided Shangluo from the north and Eastern Wei struck at Fan and Deng, Bao was made general who garrisons the south and consulting staff officer in the chancellor's office, and sent to garrison Xi and Li.

sentences.zh: 居二年，徵拜丞相府司馬，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: After two years he was summoned and appointed marshal of the chancellor's office and advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was recalled as marshal of the chancellor's office and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 出為北雍州刺史，加衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of North Yong Province and was given the added rank Great General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as inspector of North Yong Province with the added rank of great general of the guard.

sentences.zh: 州帶北山，多有盜賊。

translations.literal: The province bordered the northern mountains; bandits and robbers were many.
translations.idiomatic: The province lay along the northern hills, and banditry was widespread.

sentences.zh: 褒密訪之，並豪右所為也，而陽不之知，厚加禮遇。

translations.literal: Bao secretly investigated and found that prominent local families were behind it all, yet outwardly he pretended not to know and treated them with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Bao investigated in secret and learned that local magnates were behind the robberies, yet he feigned ignorance and treated them with marked courtesy.

sentences.zh: 謂之曰：「刺史起自書生，安知督盜，所賴卿等共分其憂耳。

translations.literal: He said to them: "The inspector rose from the ranks of lettered men — how would he know how to supervise bandits? I rely on you gentlemen to share this worry with me.
translations.idiomatic: He told them, "I am a scholar raised to office — what do I know of hunting bandits? I must rely on you to share the burden.

sentences.zh: 」乃悉詔桀黠少年素為鄉里患者，署為主帥，分其地界。

translations.literal: " He then summoned all the fierce, cunning youths who had long been a plague to their neighborhoods, appointed them chief captains, and divided the territory among them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then summoned every bold, troublesome young man who had long plagued the countryside, made them chief captains, and divided the district among them.

sentences.zh: 有盜發而不獲者，以故縱論。

translations.literal: If a robbery occurred and the culprit was not caught, they were tried on a charge of connivance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a robbery went unsolved, the captain in that sector was prosecuted for connivance.

sentences.zh: 於是諸被署者，莫不惶懼。

translations.literal: Thereupon all those appointed were filled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Every man thus appointed was seized with fear.

sentences.zh: 皆首伏曰：「前盜發者，並某等為之。

translations.literal: They all came forward and confessed: "The robberies committed before were all done by us.
translations.idiomatic: They all came forward and confessed, "Every past robbery was our work.

sentences.zh: 」所有徒侶，皆列其姓名。

translations.literal: " They listed the names of all their accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: " and gave the names of all their accomplices.

sentences.zh: 或亡命隱匿者，亦悉言其所在。

translations.literal: Even fugitives in hiding — they disclosed where each could be found.
translations.idiomatic: They even named fugitives still in hiding and told where each could be found.

sentences.zh: 褒乃取盜名簿藏之。

translations.literal: Bao then took the register of bandit names and put it away in store.
translations.idiomatic: Bao took the register of names and put it away.

sentences.zh: 因大牓州門曰：「自知行盜者，可急來首，卽除其罪。

translations.literal: He then posted a large notice at the provincial gate: "Those who know themselves to have committed robbery may hurry to come forward and confess, and their crime will at once be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then posted a large proclamation at the provincial gate: "Anyone who has committed robbery should come forward at once and his crime will be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 盡今月不首者，顯戮其身，籍沒妻子，以賞前首者。

translations.literal: All who do not confess before this month is out will be publicly executed, their wives and children registered and confiscated, as reward for those who confess first.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who fails to confess before this month ends will be executed in public, his wife and children confiscated, and their property given to those who confess first.

sentences.zh: 」旬日之間，諸盜咸悉首盡。

translations.literal: " Within ten days or so all the bandits had fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: " Within ten days every bandit had confessed.

sentences.zh: 褒取名簿勘之，一無差異。

translations.literal: Bao took out the name register and checked it — not a single discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Bao brought out the register and checked it; not one name was wrong.

sentences.zh: 竝原其罪，許以自新。

translations.literal: He pardoned their crimes altogether and allowed them to reform.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them all and allowed them to start anew.

sentences.zh: 由是羣盜屏息。

translations.literal: From this the bandit groups ceased their activity.
translations.idiomatic: After that banditry died away entirely.

sentences.zh: 入為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered service as Attendant Gentleman in Service in the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as attendant gentleman in the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷侍中。

translations.literal: In year 9 he was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 十二年，除都督、西涼州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 12 he was appointed area commander and Inspector of Western Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was appointed area commander and inspector of Western Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 羌胡之俗，輕貧弱，尚豪富。

translations.literal: Among the Qiang and Hu the custom was to despise the poor and weak and honor the rich and powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Qiang and Hu the poor and weak were despised and the rich and powerful honored.

sentences.zh: 豪富之家，侵漁小民，同於僕隸。

translations.literal: Wealthy and powerful families oppressed common folk as though they were slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families preyed on commoners as if they were bondsmen.

sentences.zh: 故貧者日削，豪者益富。

translations.literal: Thus the poor daily grew poorer and the powerful richer still.
translations.idiomatic: The poor grew poorer by the day while the powerful grew ever richer.

sentences.zh: 褒乃悉募貧人，以充兵士，優復其家，蠲免徭賦。

translations.literal: Bao then recruited the poor in full to fill out the ranks of soldiers, granting their households favorable exemption and remitting corvée and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Bao then enrolled the poor as soldiers, granted their households tax relief, and remitted corvée and levies.

sentences.zh: 又調富人財物以振給之。

translations.literal: He also assessed the property of the wealthy to relief and supply them.
translations.idiomatic: He also levied goods from wealthy households and distributed them in relief.

sentences.zh: 每西域商貨至，又先盡貧者市之。

translations.literal: Whenever merchant goods arrived from the Western Regions, he first let the poor buy them all up.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Western Region merchants arrived, he let the poor buy their goods first.

sentences.zh: 於是貧富漸均，戶口殷實。

translations.literal: Thereafter rich and poor gradually equalized, and registered households grew prosperous and solid.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually the gap between rich and poor narrowed, and the population grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 十六年，加大都督、涼州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In year 16 he was given the added title Grand Area Commander and command of all military affairs in Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he was made grand area commander with command over all military affairs in Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，轉會州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was transferred to Inspector of Hui Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was transferred to inspector of Hui Province.

sentences.zh: 二年，進位車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In year 2 his rank was advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments.

sentences.zh: 尋加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the added ranks Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening-Office Equal in Three Departments and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he received the added ranks of grand general of fast cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 武成三年，徵拜御伯中大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wucheng he was summoned and appointed middle grand master of the Office of Guardians.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 3 he was summoned and made middle grand master of the Office of Guardians.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，轉司會。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding he was transferred to director of reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 2 he was transferred to director of reckoning.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 3 he went out as Inspector of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was sent out as inspector of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 州界北接太原，當千里徑。

translations.literal: The province's border adjoined Taiyuan to the north and stood on the Thousand-li Path.
translations.idiomatic: The province bordered Taiyuan to the north and lay on the Thousand-li Path.

sentences.zh: 先是齊寇數入，民廢耕桑，前後刺史，莫能防扞。

translations.literal: Before this Northern Qi raiders had entered many times; the people abandoned farming and sericulture, and successive inspectors had none been able to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi raiders had repeatedly invaded; farming and sericulture were abandoned, and no previous inspector had been able to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 褒至，適會寇來，褒乃不下屬縣。

translations.literal: When Bao arrived, raiders happened to come; Bao therefore did not alert the subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao arrived, raiders happened to be coming, and he deliberately did not warn the subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 人旣不及設備，以故多被抄掠。

translations.literal: The people were unable to prepare in time and for that reason many were plundered.
translations.idiomatic: The people had no time to prepare and many were plundered.

sentences.zh: 齊人喜相謂曰：「汾州不覺吾至，先未集兵。

translations.literal: The men of Qi happily said to one another: "Fen Province did not notice our arrival and has not yet gathered troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi troops said to one another with delight, "Fen Province never saw us coming and has not yet mustered an army.

sentences.zh: 今者之還，必莫能追躡我矣。

translations.literal: On this return they surely cannot pursue and overtake us.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back they surely cannot catch us.

sentences.zh: 」由是益懈，不為營壘。

translations.literal: " From this they grew all the more negligent and did not build stockades.
translations.idiomatic: " So they grew careless and made no camp fortifications.

sentences.zh: 褒已先勒精銳，伏北山中，分據險阻，邀其歸路。

translations.literal: Bao had already mustered picked troops beforehand, hidden them in the northern mountains, seized the defiles, and blocked their line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had already mustered picked troops, hidden them in the northern hills, and blocked the passes on their return route.

sentences.zh: 乘其衆怠，縱伏擊之，盡獲其衆。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of their army's slackness, he released the ambush and struck; he captured the whole force.
translations.idiomatic: When their ranks had grown slack he sprang the ambush and captured the entire force.

sentences.zh: 故事，獲生口者，竝囚送京師。

translations.literal: By precedent, captives taken alive were all imprisoned and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, captives were imprisoned and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 褒因是奏曰：「所獲賊衆，不足為多。

translations.literal: Bao therefore memorialized: "The bandits captured are not so many as to matter.
translations.idiomatic: Bao therefore memorialized, "The enemy we took are too few to matter.

sentences.zh: 俘而辱之，但益其忿耳。

translations.literal: To hold prisoners and humiliate them only adds to their rage.
translations.idiomatic: To hold and humiliate them will only deepen their hatred.

sentences.zh: 請一切放還，以德報怨。

translations.literal: I ask that they all be released, returning good for ill.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they all be sent home, repaying injury with kindness.

sentences.zh: 」有詔許焉。

translations.literal: " An edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 自此抄兵頗息。

translations.literal: From this raiding forces largely ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After that the border raids largely ceased.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷河洮封三州諸軍事、河州總管。

translations.literal: In year 4 he was transferred to command of military affairs for the three provinces He, Tao, and Feng and made area commander of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was given command of military affairs in He, Tao, and Feng and made area commander of He Province.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，轉鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe he was transferred to Inspector of Feng Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 3 he was transferred to inspector of Feng Province.

sentences.zh: 尋以年老請致仕，詔許之。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of old age, he requested retirement; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, citing old age, he asked to retire, and an edict allowed it.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜少保。

translations.literal: In year 5 he was appointed Lesser Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was appointed lesser preceptor.

sentences.zh: 褒歷事三帝，以忠厚見知。

translations.literal: Bao served three emperors and was known for steadfast loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Through the reigns of three emperors, Bao earned renown for unwavering fidelity.

sentences.zh: 高祖深相敬重，常以師道處之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu deeply respected him and habitually treated him with the courtesy due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu held him in deep respect and always treated him with the courtesy due a teacher.

sentences.zh: 每入朝見，必有詔令坐，然後始與論政事。

translations.literal: Whenever he came to audience there was always an edict ordering him to be seated before discussion of state affairs began.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to court an edict always bade him sit before affairs of state were discussed.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In year 7 he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 7.

sentences.zh: 贈涇岐燕三州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the three provincial inspectorates of Jing, Qi, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made inspector of Jing, Qi, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子繼伯嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jibo succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jibo inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 趙肅字慶雍，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Su, styled Qingyong, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Su, courtesy name Qingyong, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 世居河西。

translations.literal: For generations the family dwelt west of the River.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had lived west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 及沮渠氏滅，曾祖武始歸於魏，賜爵金城侯。

translations.literal: When the Juqu clan was destroyed, his great-grandfather Wushi submitted to Wei and was granted Marquis of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Juqu were overthrown, his great-grandfather Wushi came over to Wei and was enfeoffed marquis of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 祖興，中書博士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xing was an erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xing served as an erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父申侯，舉秀才，後軍府主簿。

translations.literal: His father Shenhou passed the provincial examination, and served as chief clerk in the Rear Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shenhou passed the provincial examination and served as chief clerk in the rear army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 肅早有操行，知名於時。

translations.literal: Su from early on had conduct and integrity and was renowned in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Su had shown integrity from youth and was well known in his day.

sentences.zh: 魏正光五年，酈元為河南尹，辟肅為主簿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang of Wei, Li Yuan became Administrator of Henan and recruited Su as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei's Zhengguang year 5, Li Yuan became administrator of Henan and recruited Su as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，起家殿中侍御史，加威烈將軍、奉朝請、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he first entered office as Palace Attendant Censor, given the added ranks General Who Inspires Awe, attendant at court audiences, and acting attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he began his career as palace attendant censor, with the added ranks of general who inspires awe, attendant at court audiences, and acting attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋除直後，轉直寢。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed direct attendant and transferred to direct attendant of the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made direct attendant and then transferred to direct attendant of the inner chamber.

sentences.zh: 永安初，授廷尉

translations.literal: At the opening of Yong'an he was appointed director of justice
translations.idiomatic: With the Yong'an era's dawn, he took office as director of justice

translations.literal: (Tian) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Tian]

sentences.zh: 平，二年，轉監。

translations.literal: ping; in year 2 he was transferred to overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianping, in year 2 he was transferred to overseer.

sentences.zh: 後以母憂去職，起為廷尉正。

translations.literal: Later, because of mourning for his mother, he left office; he was recalled and made rectifier of the directorate of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Later he left office to mourn his mother, then was recalled and made rectifier of the directorate of justice.

sentences.zh: 以疾免。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 久之，授征虜將軍、中散大夫，遷左將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: After a long while he was given General Who Campaigns against Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Leisure, then transferred to Left General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he received the ranks of general who campaigns against barbarians and grand master of palace leisure, then was made left general and grand master of palace counsel.

sentences.zh: 東魏天平初，除新安郡守。

translations.literal: At the opening of Tianping in Eastern Wei he was appointed Administrator of Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Eastern Wei's Tianping era he was appointed administrator of Xin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，還洛。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，獨孤信東討，肅率宗人為鄉導。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Dugu Xin campaigned east; Su led clansmen as local guides.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 3, when Dugu Xin marched east, Su led his clansmen as local guides.

sentences.zh: 授司州治中，轉別駕。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice-prefect of Si Province and transferred to chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice-prefect of Si Province and then made chief aide.

sentences.zh: 監督糧儲，軍用不匱。

translations.literal: He supervised grain stores, and military supplies did not run short.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw grain stores so that the army never lacked supplies.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，謂人曰：「趙肅可謂洛陽主人也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard of it and said to people: "Zhao Su may truly be called master of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai heard of it he told others, "Zhao Su is truly master of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 」七年，加鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫、都督，仍別駕。

translations.literal: " In year 7 he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the South, Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, and area commander, while retaining his post as vice-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was further made general who pacifies the south, grand master of golden seal and purple girdle, and area commander, and kept his post as vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 領所部義徒，據守大塢。

translations.literal: He led his volunteer followers and held the great stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He led his volunteer militia and held the great stockade.

sentences.zh: 又兼行臺左丞，東道慰勞。

translations.literal: He also concurrently served as left director of the mobile headquarters and was sent to comfort and reward the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as left director of the mobile headquarters and went east to comfort and reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 九年，行華山郡事。

translations.literal: In year 9 he acted as administrator of Huashan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In his ninth year of service, he governed Huashan commandery in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 十三年，除廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: In year 13 he was appointed vice-director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: By year thirteen he had risen to vice-director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 明年元日，當行朝禮，非有封爵者，不得預焉。

translations.literal: The next year, on New Year's Day, the court ceremony was to be held; those without enfeoffment could not take part.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on New Year's Day, the court ceremony was held, and those without a fief could not attend.

sentences.zh: 肅時未有茅土。

translations.literal: At the time Su had not yet received a fief.
translations.idiomatic: Su had not yet received any enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 左僕射長孫儉白太祖請之。

translations.literal: Left vice-director Changsun Jian informed Grand Progenitor and requested one for him.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice-director Changsun Jian reported this to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and asked that Su be enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃召肅謂曰：「歲初行禮，豈得使卿不預，然何為不早言也？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor thereupon summoned Su and said to him: "At the opening rites of the year, how could I leave you out? Yet why did you not speak up earlier?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then summoned Su and said, "At the year's opening ceremony, how could I leave you out? But why did you not say so sooner?

sentences.zh: 」於是令肅自選封名。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he had Su choose his own enfeoffment name.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had Su choose the name of his own fief.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「河清乃太平之應，竊所願也。

translations.literal: Su said: "When rivers run clear it is a sign of great peace — that is what I privately wish for.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "When rivers run clear it is a portent of peace — that is what I have long wished for.

sentences.zh: 」於是封清河縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was enfeoffed Viscount of Qinghe county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " He was therefore enfeoffed as viscount of Qinghe county with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十六年，除廷尉卿，加征東將軍。

translations.literal: In year 16 he was appointed director of the Court of Justice and additionally made General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he was made director of the Court of Justice and additionally general who campaigns east.

sentences.zh: 肅久在理官，執心平允。

translations.literal: Su had long served as a judicial official; his handling of cases was fair and even.
translations.idiomatic: Su had long served in the judiciary, and his judgments were fair and even-handed.

sentences.zh: 凡所處斷，咸得其情。

translations.literal: In every case he decided, he grasped the true circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: In every case he decided, he got to the truth of the matter.

sentences.zh: 廉慎自居，不營產業。

translations.literal: He maintained himself in integrity and caution and did not build up property.
translations.idiomatic: He lived with integrity and restraint and did not accumulate property.

sentences.zh: 時人以此稱之。

translations.literal: People of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進位車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍，賜姓乙弗氏。

translations.literal: In year 17 he was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and was granted the surname Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he was promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and regular attendant of scattered cavalry, and was granted the surname Yifu.

sentences.zh: 先是，太祖命肅撰定法律。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Progenitor had ordered Su to compile and fix the laws.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had ordered Su to draft and codify the laws.

sentences.zh: 肅積思累年，遂感心疾。

translations.literal: Su pondered deeply for many years and consequently developed a heart ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Su brooded over the task for years and eventually developed a heart ailment.

sentences.zh: 去職，卒於家。

translations.literal: He left office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned from office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子正禮，齊王憲府屬、大都督、新安郡守。

translations.literal: His son Zhengli served as staff member in the household of Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian, grand area commander, and administrator of Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengli served on the staff of Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian, as grand area commander and administrator of Xin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 時有高平徐招少好法律。

translations.literal: At the time there was Xu Zhao of Gaoping, who from youth loved the law.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Xu Zhao of Gaoping, who from youth had loved the law.

sentences.zh: 發言措筆，常欲辨析秋毫。

translations.literal: In speech and in writing he always sought to distinguish the finest points.
translations.idiomatic: In speech and writing he always tried to split the finest hairs.

sentences.zh: 歷職內外，有當官之譽。

translations.literal: Through offices both within and outside the capital he earned the reputation of a capable official.
translations.idiomatic: In posts inside and outside the capital alike he won a reputation as a capable official.

sentences.zh: 從魏孝武入關，為給事黃門侍郎、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei into Guanzhong and served as Attendant in the Yellow Gate and Right Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei into Guanzhong and served as attendant in the Yellow Gate and right vice-director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷播遷，典章有闕，至於臺閣軌儀，多招所參定。

translations.literal: At the time the court was in exile and institutions were incomplete; as for the protocols of the central offices, Zhao largely participated in fixing them.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then in exile and institutions were incomplete; Zhao took a leading part in setting the protocols of the central offices.

sentences.zh: 論者稱之。

translations.literal: Commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries and critics alike spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中、度支尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to palace attendant and director of revenue.

sentences.zh: 大統初，卒。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Datong era he died.

sentences.zh: 張軌字元軌，濟北臨邑人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, styled Yuangui, was a native of Linyi in Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, courtesy name Yuangui, came from Linyi in Jibei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父崇，高平令。

translations.literal: His father Chong was magistrate of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong had served as magistrate of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 軌少好學，志識開朗。

translations.literal: Gui from youth loved learning; his aims and understanding were broad and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Gui loved learning from youth, and his aims and judgment were broad and clear.

sentences.zh: 初在洛陽，家貧，與樂安孫樹仁為莫逆之友，每易衣而出。

translations.literal: When he was first in Luoyang, his family was poor; he and Sun Shuren of Le'an were the closest of friends, and they would take turns wearing each other's clothes when going out.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first in Luoyang his family was poor; he and Sun Shuren of Le'an were inseparable friends and would take turns wearing each other's clothes when they went out.

sentences.zh: 以此見稱。

translations.literal: For this he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was admired.

sentences.zh: 永安中，隨爾朱榮擊元顥，除討寇將軍、奉朝請。

translations.literal: During Yongan he followed Erzhu Rong in attacking Yuan Hao and was appointed General Who Punishes Bandits and Court Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongan era he followed Erzhu Rong against Yuan Hao and was made general who punishes bandits and court attendant.

sentences.zh: 軌常謂所親曰：「秦雍之間，必有王者。

translations.literal: Gui often said to those close to him: "Between Qin and Yong there will surely be a king.
translations.idiomatic: Gui often told those close to him, "Between Qin and Yong there is bound to be a king.

sentences.zh: 」爾朱氏敗後，遂杖策入關。

translations.literal: " After the Erzhu clan fell, he took staff in hand and entered Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: " After the Erzhu house fell, he took staff in hand and entered Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳以軌為記室參軍，典機務。

translations.literal: He Ba Yue made Gui his secretariat adjutant in charge of critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He Ba Yue made Gui his secretariat adjutant and put him in charge of critical affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋轉倉曹，加鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to granary affairs and was given the added rank of General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to granary affairs and given the added rank of general who pacifies the distant.

sentences.zh: 時穀糴湧貴，或有請貸官倉者。

translations.literal: At the time grain prices surged; some asked to borrow from the official granary.
translations.idiomatic: Grain prices were then soaring, and some asked to borrow from the official granary.

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「以私害公，非吾宿志。

translations.literal: Gui said: "To harm the public for private gain is not my longstanding intent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "To harm the public for private gain has never been my intent.

sentences.zh: 濟人之難，詎得相違。

translations.literal: To relieve people in difficulty — how could I refuse?
translations.idiomatic: To help people in distress — how could I refuse?

sentences.zh: 」乃賣所服衣物，糴粟以賑其乏。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sold his own clothing, bought grain, and relieved their want.
translations.idiomatic: " He sold his own clothes, bought grain, and relieved their distress.

sentences.zh: 及岳被害，太祖以軌為都督，從征侯莫陳悅。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed, Grand Progenitor made Gui area commander and he followed in the campaign against Hou Mo Chen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue was killed, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai made Gui area commander and he followed the campaign against Hou Mo Chen Yue.

sentences.zh: 悅平，使於洛陽。

translations.literal: When Yue was pacified, he was sent on mission to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yue was defeated, he was sent on mission to Luoyong.

sentences.zh: 見領軍斛斯椿，椿曰：「高歡逆謀，已傳行路。

translations.literal: He met the army commander Husu Chun. Chun said: "Gao Huan's rebellious plot is already known on every road.
translations.idiomatic: He met the army commander Husu Chun, who said, "Gao Huan's treason is already common talk on every road.

sentences.zh: 人情西望，以日為年。

translations.literal: People's hearts look west; they count the days like years.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts turn westward, and men count the days like years.

sentences.zh: 未知宇文何如賀拔也？

translations.literal: Who knows whether Yuwen can compare with He Ba?
translations.idiomatic: Who knows whether Yuwen can measure up to He Ba?

sentences.zh: 」軌曰：「宇文公文足經國，武可定亂。

translations.literal: Gui said: "Master Yuwen's letters are sufficient to govern the state; his martial prowess can quell disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "Master Yuwen's civil talent is enough to govern the realm, and his martial prowess can settle chaos.

sentences.zh: 至於高識遠度，非愚管所測。

translations.literal: As for his lofty insight and far-reaching judgment, that is not something my dull measure can fathom.
translations.idiomatic: As for his lofty vision and far-reaching judgment, that is beyond my poor reckoning.

sentences.zh: 」椿曰：「誠如卿言，真可恃也。

translations.literal: " Chun said: "If it is truly as you say, he can indeed be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: " Chun said, "If that is truly so, he can indeed be relied on.

sentences.zh: 」太祖為行臺，授軌郎中。

translations.literal: " Grand Progenitor became mobile headquarters; Gui was appointed gentleman-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai became mobile headquarters, Gui was appointed gentleman-attendant.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，除中書舍人，封壽張縣子，邑三百戶，加左將軍、濟州大中正，兼著作佐郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Gui was appointed secretariat drafting officer, enfeoffed Viscount of Shouzhang with a fief of three hundred households, given Left General and Grand Rectifier of Ji Province, and concurrently associate drafting officer compiling the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Gui was made secretariat drafting officer, enfeoffed as viscount of Shouzhang with a fief of three hundred households, given the added ranks of left general and grand rectifier of Ji Province, and concurrently associate drafting officer compiling the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant in the Yellow Gate and concurrently director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant in the Yellow Gate and concurrently director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 六年，出為河北郡守。

translations.literal: In year 6 he went out as administrator of Hebei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Six years on, he was posted as administrator of Hebei commandery.

sentences.zh: 在郡三年，聲績甚著。

translations.literal: During three years in the commandery his reputation and achievements were very outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: During three years in the commandery his reputation and achievements were outstanding.

sentences.zh: 臨人治術，有循吏之美。

translations.literal: In governing the people he had the qualities of an exemplary official.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the people he showed the virtues of an exemplary official.

sentences.zh: 大統間，宰人者多推尚之。

translations.literal: During Datong, many who held district office recommended and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era many local administrators recommended and admired him.

sentences.zh: 入為丞相府從事中郎，行武功郡事。

translations.literal: He entered service as attendant in the chancellor's office and acted for Wu Gong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as attendant in the chancellor's office and acted as administrator of Wu Gong commandery.

sentences.zh: 章武公導出鎮

translations.literal: Duke of Zhangwu Dao went out to govern
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Zhangwu Yuwen Dao went out to govern

translations.literal: (Tai) [emended: Qin]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Qin]

sentences.zh: 〔秦〕州，以軌為長史。

translations.literal: Qin Province, Gui was made chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Zhangwu Yuwen Dao went out to govern Qin Province, Gui was made chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 加撫軍將軍、大都督、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was given the added ranks of General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Area Commander, and Direct Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the added ranks of general who pacifies the army, grand area commander, and direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In year 1 of Emperor Fei of Wei he was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 二年，賜姓宇文氏，行南秦州事。

translations.literal: In year 2 he was granted the surname Yuwen and acted for Southern Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he received the surname Yuwen and governed Southern Qin Province in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，徵拜度支尚書，復除隴右府長史。

translations.literal: In year 2 of Emperor Gong of Wei he was summoned as Director of Revenue and again appointed chief clerk of the Longyou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was summoned as director of revenue and again appointed chief clerk of the Longyou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 卒於位，時年五十五。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died still in office, aged fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 諡曰質。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zhi.

sentences.zh: 軌性清素，臨終之日，家無餘財，唯有素書數百卷。

translations.literal: Gui's nature was plain and austere; on the day of his death the household had no surplus wealth — only several hundred volumes of plain books.
translations.idiomatic: Gui lived plainly and simply; on the day he died his household had no surplus wealth — only several hundred volumes of unadorned books.

sentences.zh: 子肅，世宗初，為宣納上士，轉中外府記室參軍、中山公訓侍讀。

translations.literal: His son Su, at the start of Shizong's reign, was Upper Gentleman Who Receives Petitions; he was transferred to secretariat adjutant of the Central and External Office and tutor to Duke of Zhongshan Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su, at the start of Emperor Ming's reign, was upper gentleman who receives petitions; he was transferred to secretariat adjutant of the central and external office and tutor to Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Xun.

sentences.zh: 早有才名，性頗輕猾，時人比之魏諷。

translations.literal: He had early talent and renown; his character was rather frivolous and slippery; people of the time compared him to Wei Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He had early talent and fame, but his character was rather frivolous and slippery, and people of the time compared him to Wei Feng.

sentences.zh: 卒以罪考竟終。

translations.literal: He died at the end of a criminal interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He died under criminal interrogation.

sentences.zh: 李彥字彥士，梁郡下邑人也。

translations.literal: Li Yan, styled Yanshi, was a native of Xiayi in Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, courtesy name Yanshi, came from Xiayi in Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖先之，魏淮南郡守。

translations.literal: Ancestor Xianzhi was administrator of Huainan commandery in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Xianzhi had served Wei as administrator of Huainan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父靜，南青州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jing was inspector of Southern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing had served as inspector of Southern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 彥少有節操，好學慕古，為鄉閭之所敬憚。

translations.literal: Yan from youth had integrity, loved learning and admired antiquity; his hometown both respected and stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had integrity from youth, loved learning and admired antiquity, and was respected and feared in his home district.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，解褐奉朝請，加輕車將軍。

translations.literal: During Xiaochang he left the cloth and became Court Attendant, with the added rank of General of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he entered service as court attendant and was given the added rank of general of light chariots.

sentences.zh: 從魏孝武入關，兼著作佐郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei into Guanzhong, concurrently associate drafting officer compiling the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei into Guanzhong and served concurrently as associate drafting officer compiling the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 加寧朔將軍，進號冠軍將軍、中散大夫，遷平東將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was given the added rank of General Who Pacifies the North; advanced to General Who Gains the Victory and Palace Regular Grand Master; transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master for Palace Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the added rank of general who pacifies the north, advanced to general who gains the victory and palace regular grand master, and transferred to general who pacifies the east and grand master for palace discussion.

sentences.zh: 大統初，除通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong he was appointed Direct Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Datong era he was appointed direct attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜安東將軍、銀青光祿大夫、太保轉太傅長史、儀曹郎中、左民郎中。

translations.literal: In year 3 he was made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Silver Seal and Blue Girdle, chief clerk when the Grand Tutor replaced the Grand Mentor, director in the Bureau of Ceremonies, and director in the Bureau of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made general who pacifies the east, grand master of silver seal and blue girdle, chief clerk when the grand tutor replaced the grand mentor, director in the Bureau of Ceremonies, and director in the Bureau of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 十二年，省三十六曹為十二部，改授民部郎中，封平陽縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In year 12, when the thirty-six bureaus were reduced to twelve departments, he was reassigned as director in the Bureau of the People, enfeoffed Viscount of Pingyang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, when the thirty-six bureaus were consolidated into twelve departments, he was reassigned as director in the Bureau of the People and enfeoffed as viscount of Pingyang with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十五年，進號中軍將軍，兼尚書左丞，領選部。

translations.literal: In year 15 he was advanced to Central Army General, concurrently left vice-director of the Masters of Writing, and put in charge of the selection bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was advanced to central army general, made left vice-director of the Masters of Writing concurrently, and put in charge of the selection bureau.

sentences.zh: 大軍東討，加持節、大都督、通直散騎常侍，掌留臺事。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned east, he was given the staff of authority, made Grand Area Commander and Direct Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and put in charge of affairs at the capital while the court was away.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army campaigned east, he was given the staff of authority, made grand area commander and direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, and put in charge of the capital administration while the court was in the field.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝初，拜尚書右丞，轉左丞。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Fei of Wei he was appointed right vice-director of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to left vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Fei of Wei's reign he was appointed right vice-director of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to left vice-director.

sentences.zh: 彥在尚書十有五載，屬軍國草創，庶務殷繁，留心省閱，未嘗懈怠。

translations.literal: Yan served in the Masters of Writing for fifteen years; as the army-state was being founded and routine business was heavy, he reviewed documents with care and never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Yan served in the Masters of Writing for fifteen years; as the army-state was being founded and business was heavy, he reviewed documents with care and never slackened.

sentences.zh: 斷決如流，略無疑滯。

translations.literal: Decisions flowed from him; scarcely any case hung in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: His decisions flowed like water, and scarcely any case hung in doubt.

sentences.zh: 臺閣莫不歎其公勤，服其明察。

translations.literal: None in the central offices failed to marvel at his diligence and fairness, and to admire his sharp judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the central offices marveled at his diligence and admired his sharp judgment.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，仍左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant in the Yellow Gate while retaining the left vice-directorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant in the Yellow Gate while retaining the left vice-directorship.

sentences.zh: 尋進車騎大將軍、儀同三司，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 出為鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as inspector of Fu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as inspector of Fu Province.

sentences.zh: 彥以東夏未平，固辭州任，詔許之。

translations.literal: Yan, because Eastern Xia was not yet pacified, firmly declined the provincial post; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Because Eastern Xia was not yet pacified, Yan firmly declined the provincial appointment, and an edict approved.

sentences.zh: 拜兵部尚書，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，仍兼著作。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of War, given the added ranks of Flying-Cavalry Grand General and Opening-Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and still concurrently served in the drafting office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of war, given the added ranks of flying-cavalry grand general and opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and still served concurrently in the drafting office.

sentences.zh: 六官建，改授軍司馬，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was reassigned as army marshal and raised to count.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were reorganized, he became army marshal and was raised to count.

sentences.zh: 彥性謙恭，有禮節。
