translations.literal: Yan's nature was humble and courteous, with proper ritual bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was humble and courteous by nature and observed proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 雖居顯要，於親黨之間，恂恂如也。

translations.literal: Though he held eminent rank, among kin and associates he was deferential and modest.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held high office, among kin and friends he was deferential and modest.

sentences.zh: 輕財重義，好施愛士。

translations.literal: He valued righteousness over wealth, loved to give, and cherished scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He valued righteousness over wealth, loved to give, and cherished men of talent.

sentences.zh: 時論以此稱之。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 然素多疾而勤於莅職，雖沉頓枕席，猶理務不輟，遂至於卒。

translations.literal: Yet he had long been ill yet was diligent in office; even confined to his sickbed he did not cease handling affairs, until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had long been ill and still attended diligently to his duties; even bedridden he did not stop handling affairs, until at last he died.

sentences.zh: 時年四十六。

translations.literal: At the time he was forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-six at the time.

sentences.zh: 諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jing.

sentences.zh: 彥臨終遺誡其子等曰：「昔人以窾木為櫝，葛虆為緘，下不亂泉，上不泄臭。

translations.literal: Yan on his deathbed left instruction to his sons and the rest, saying: "Formerly men used hollow wood as a coffin and vine wraps as bindings; below they did not disturb the springs, above they did not leak foul odor.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Yan admonished his sons, saying, "Men of old used hollow logs for coffins and vine for bindings, so that the waters below were not fouled and no stench rose above.

sentences.zh: 此實吾平生之志也。

translations.literal: This truly was my aspiration throughout life.
translations.idiomatic: That was truly the way I wished to live my whole life.

sentences.zh: 但事旣矯枉，恐為世士所譏。

translations.literal: But the matter has already overcorrected; I fear being ridiculed by gentlemen of the age.
translations.idiomatic: But I have already lived contrary to the norm and fear that men of the world will mock me.

sentences.zh: 今可斂以時服，葬於磽塉之地，忽用明器、芻塗及儀衛等。

translations.literal: Now you may enclose me in ordinary dress, bury me in barren stony ground, and do not use spirit objects, straw and earth mounds, ceremonial guards, or the like.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, dress me in plain clothes, bury me in stony waste ground, and do not use spirit objects, grave ornaments, escorts of honor, or anything like them.

sentences.zh: 爾其念之。

translations.literal: You must keep this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: See that you remember this.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷嘉焉，不奪其志。

translations.literal: " The court commended this and did not overrule his wish.
translations.idiomatic: " The court praised this and did not override his wishes.

sentences.zh: 子升明嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shengming succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shengming inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 少歷顯職。

translations.literal: From youth he passed through prominent offices.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he held several high posts.

sentences.zh: 大象末，太府中大夫、儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang he held the ranks of palace grandee of the grand treasury and equal-protocol grand general.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daxiang era he held the ranks of palace grandee of the grand treasury and equal-protocol grand general.

sentences.zh: 郭彥，太原陽曲人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yan was a native of Yangqu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yan came from Yangqu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 其先從宦關右，遂居馮翊。

translations.literal: His ancestors followed official careers in Guanxi and then settled in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had followed official careers in Guanxi and then settled in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父胤，郡功曹、靈武令。

translations.literal: His father Yin was commandery merit officer and magistrate of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin had served as commandery merit officer and magistrate of Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐祚，出為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was sent out as Inspector of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Guo Yan was sent out as inspector of Li Province.

sentences.zh: 蠻左生梗，未遵朝憲。

translations.literal: The tribal peoples of the region were stubborn and did not observe court law.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples of the region were recalcitrant and paid little heed to imperial law.

sentences.zh: 至於賦稅，違命者多。

translations.literal: As for taxes and levies, many disobeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Many refused to pay the taxes and levies demanded of them.

sentences.zh: 聚散無恆，不營農業。

translations.literal: They gathered and dispersed without fixed pattern and did not engage in agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: They roamed without settled lives and did not farm.

sentences.zh: 彥勸以耕稼，禁共遊獵，民皆務本，家有餘糧。

translations.literal: Yan urged them toward farming, forbade shared hunting expeditions, and all the people devoted themselves to the root occupation; households had surplus grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yan urged them to farm, forbade communal hunting, and the people turned to agriculture until every household had grain to spare.

sentences.zh: 亡命之徒，咸從賦役。

translations.literal: Fugitives all submitted to tax and corvée service.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives came back under tax and corvée alike.

sentences.zh: 先是以澧州糧儲乏少，每令荊州遞送。

translations.literal: Previously because Li Province's grain stores were deficient, Jing Province was always ordered to relay supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Li Province had lacked grain stores, and Jing Province had to relay supplies to it.

sentences.zh: 自彥蒞職，倉庾充實，無復轉輸之勞。

translations.literal: From the time Yan took office, the granaries were full and there was no further labor of relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan took office the granaries were full and the burden of relay transport ended.

sentences.zh: 齊南安城主馮顯密遣使歸降，其衆未之知也。

translations.literal: Qi commander of Nan'an city Feng Xian secretly sent envoys to surrender; his troops did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xian, Qi commander of Nan'an, secretly sent envoys to surrender, but his troops knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 柱國宇文貴令彥率兵應接。

translations.literal: Pillar-general Yuwen Gui ordered Yan to lead troops to meet and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar-general Yuwen Gui ordered Yan to lead troops to meet him.

sentences.zh: 齊人先令顯率所部送糧南下，彥懼其衆不從命，乃於路邀之。

translations.literal: The Qi men first ordered Xian to lead his command south to deliver grain; Yan feared the troops would not obey, and so waylaid them on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi first ordered Xian to lead his command south with grain; Yan feared the men would not obey and waylaid them on the road.

sentences.zh: 顯因得自拔。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon was able to escape on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was thus able to escape.

sentences.zh: 其衆果拒戰，彥縱兵奮擊，並虜獲之。

translations.literal: His troops indeed resisted battle; Yan unleashed his troops in fierce attack and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: The troops resisted, but Yan attacked fiercely and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 以南安無備，卽引軍掩襲。

translations.literal: Because Nan'an had no preparations, he immediately led his army in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an was unprepared, so he immediately led his army in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 顯外兵參軍鄒紹旣為彥所獲，因請為鄉導。

translations.literal: Xian's external troops staff officer Zou Shao had already been captured by Yan and thereupon asked to serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Shao, external-troops staff officer under Xian, had already been captured by Yan and offered to serve as guide.

sentences.zh: 彥遂夜至城下，令紹詐稱顯歸。

translations.literal: Yan then reached the city by night and ordered Shao to falsely claim Xian had returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan reached the city by night and had Shao claim that Xian had returned.

sentences.zh: 門者開門待之，彥引兵而入，遂有其城。

translations.literal: The gate guards opened the gate to await them; Yan led his troops inside and thereby possessed the city.
translations.idiomatic: The gate guards opened the gate to admit them; Yan led his troops inside and took the city.

sentences.zh: 俘獲三千餘人。

translations.literal: Captives numbered more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He took more than three thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 晉公護嘉之，進爵懷德縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu commended this and advanced his enfeoffment to Duke of Huaide county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu commended this and raised him to duke of Huaide county with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以南安懸遠，尋令班師。

translations.literal: Because Nan'an was dangerously distant, he was soon ordered to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Because Nan'an was too far to hold, he was soon ordered to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 及秩滿還朝，民吏號泣送彥二百餘裏。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned to court, officials and people wept and escorted Yan for more than two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to court, officials and commoners wept and escorted him for more than two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 尋為東道大使，觀省風俗。

translations.literal: Soon he was made eastern-route commissioner to inspect local customs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed eastern-route commissioner to tour and assess local customs.

sentences.zh: 除蒲州總管府長史，入為工部中大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief administrator of Pu Province overall headquarters; he entered court as grand master in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief administrator of Pu Province overall headquarters, then entered court as grand master in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，護東討。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, Hu undertook an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 4 Yuwen Hu undertook an eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 彥從尉遲迥攻洛陽。

translations.literal: Yan followed Yuchi Jiong in attacking Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan followed Yuchi Jiong in the attack on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 迥復令彥與權景宣南出汝潁。

translations.literal: Jiong again ordered Yan and Quan Jingxuan south through Ru and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong then ordered Yan and Quan Jingxuan south through Ru and Ying.

sentences.zh: 及軍次豫州，彥請攻之。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Yu Province, Yan requested to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Yu Province, Yan asked to attack it.

sentences.zh: 景宣以城守旣嚴，卒難攻取，將欲南轅，更圖經略。

translations.literal: Jingxuan, because the city garrison was already strict, said it would be difficult to storm and take; he intended to turn south and reconsider strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan thought the garrison too strong to storm and intended to turn south and reconsider strategy.

sentences.zh: 彥以奉命出師，須與大軍相接。

translations.literal: Yan said that having been ordered to march out, they must link up with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Yan argued that, having been ordered out on campaign, they had to link up with the main army.

sentences.zh: 若向江畔立功，更非朝廷本意。

translations.literal: If they sought merit along the riverbank, that would be even further from the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: To win glory along the river would stray even further from the court's intent.

sentences.zh: 固執不從，兼畫攻取之計。

translations.literal: He stubbornly would not comply and also outlined a plan for storming and taking the city.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to yield and also outlined a plan to storm the city.

sentences.zh: 會其刺史王士良妻弟董遠秀密遣送款，景宣乃從。

translations.literal: It happened that the prefect's wife's younger brother Dong Yuanxiu secretly sent word of surrender; Jingxuan thereupon consented.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the prefect's brother-in-law Dong Yuanxiu secretly offered to surrender, and Jingxuan consented.

sentences.zh: 於是引軍圍之，士良遂出降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the army to invest it, and Shiliang thereupon came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He then invested the city, and Wang Shiliang came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 仍以彥鎮豫州，增邑六百戶。

translations.literal: Yan was again left to garrison Yu Province, with fief increased by six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was left to garrison Yu Province, and his fief was increased by six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋以洛陽班師，亦棄而不守。

translations.literal: Soon, because of withdrawal from Luoyang, it was also abandoned without being held.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, when the army withdrew from Luoyang, Yu Province was abandoned as well.

sentences.zh: 屬純州刺史樊舍卒，其地旣東接陳境，俗兼蠻左，初喪州將，境內騷然。

translations.literal: At this time the prefect of Chun prefecture Fan She died; the region bordered Chen on the east and its customs mixed with tribal peoples; when the provincial commander first died, the territory was suddenly unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan She, prefect of Chun, died, the region—bordering Chen on the east and mixing tribal custom with Han ways—was thrown into unrest at the loss of its commander.

sentences.zh: 朝議以彥威信著于東南，便令鎮撫。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that Yan's authority and reputation were well established in the southeast and therefore ordered him to garrison and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that Yan's authority was well established in the southeast and ordered him to garrison and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 彥至，吏人畏而愛之。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived, officials and people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan took up his post, magistrates and commoners alike both feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 天和元年，除益州總管府長史，轉隴右總管府長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, he was appointed chief administrator of Yi Province overall headquarters and transferred to chief administrator of Longyou overall headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 1 he was appointed chief administrator of Yi Province overall headquarters and transferred to chief administrator of Longyou overall headquarters.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈小司空、宜鄜丹三州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given lesser minister of works and the three inspectorates of Yi, Fu, and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made lesser minister of works and inspector of Yi, Fu, and Dan provinces.

sentences.zh: 裴文舉字道裕，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Wenju, styled Daoyu, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wenju, courtesy name Daoyu, came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖秀業，魏中散大夫、天水郡守，贈平州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiuye was Wei palace attendant cavalier at leisure and administrator of Tianshui commandery, posthumously given Inspector of Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiuye had served Wei as attendant cavalier at leisure and administrator of Tianshui commandery and was posthumously made inspector of Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 父邃，性方嚴，為州里所推挹。

translations.literal: His father Sui by nature was upright and stern and was admired and respected by his province and village.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui was upright and stern by nature and was admired throughout his province and home district.

sentences.zh: 解褐散騎常侍、奉車都尉，累遷諫議大夫、司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: On leaving common cloth he was attendant cavalier at leisure and commander who escorts chariots; through successive promotions he reached remonstrance and counsel grand master and staff officer in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as attendant cavalier at leisure and commander who escorts chariots, then rose through remonstrance and counsel grand master to staff officer in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，東魏來寇，邃乃糾合鄉人，分據險要以自固。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Eastern Wei came raiding; Sui thereupon gathered fellow villagers and divided them to hold strategic passes and defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 3, when Eastern Wei raided, Sui rallied his fellow villagers and divided them to hold strategic passes and defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 時東魏以正平為東雍州，遣其將司馬恭鎮之。

translations.literal: At the time Eastern Wei made Zhengping Eastern Yong Province and sent its general Sima Gong to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei had made Zhengping into Eastern Yong Province and posted its general Sima Gong there.

sentences.zh: 每遣間人，扇動百姓。

translations.literal: They repeatedly sent agents to incite the common people.
translations.idiomatic: They repeatedly sent agents to stir up the people.

sentences.zh: 邃密遣都督韓僧明入城，喻其將士，卽有五百餘人，許為內應。

translations.literal: Sui secretly sent area commander Han Sengming into the city to persuade its officers and soldiers; more than five hundred men at once agreed to serve as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Sui secretly sent area commander Han Sengming into the city to win over the garrison, and more than five hundred men at once agreed to act as inside collaborators.

sentences.zh: 期日未至，恭知之，乃棄城夜走。

translations.literal: Before the appointed day arrived, Gong learned of it and thereupon abandoned the city and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Before the day set for the rising, Gong learned of the plot, abandoned the city, and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 因是東雍遂內屬。

translations.literal: Because of this Eastern Yong thereupon submitted internally.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yong thereupon submitted to Zhou rule.

sentences.zh: 及李弼略地東境，邃為之鄉導，多所降下。

translations.literal: When Li Bi overran the eastern borders, Sui served as his guide, and many places surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bi overran the eastern borderlands, Sui served as his guide and many places surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，特賞衣物，封澄城縣子，邑三百戶，進安東將軍、銀青光祿大夫，加散騎常侍、太尉府司馬，除正平郡守。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor commended this and specially rewarded him with clothing; enfeoffed as Viscount of Chengcheng county with a fief of three hundred households; promoted to general who pacifies the east and silver-crown grand master of splendid happiness; given the added ranks of attendant cavalier at leisure and marshal of the Grand Commandant's headquarters; appointed administrator of Zhengping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai commended this and specially rewarded him with clothing, enfeoffed him as viscount of Chengcheng county with a fief of three hundred households, promoted him to general who pacifies the east and silver-crown grand master of splendid happiness, made him attendant cavalier at leisure and marshal of the grand commandant's headquarters, and appointed him administrator of Zhengping commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈儀同三司、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given equal in protocol to the three excellencies and Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers and inspector of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 文舉少忠謹，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Wenju from youth was loyal and careful and ranged broadly through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju was loyal and careful from youth and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 大統十年，起家奉朝請，遷丞相府墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Datong he began his career as court attendant and was transferred to ink-bureau staff officer in the chancellor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 10 he entered service as court attendant and was transferred to ink-bureau staff officer in the chancellor's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時太祖諸子年幼，盛簡賓友。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Progenitor's sons were young and carefully selected guest companions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's sons were young, and companions for them were chosen with care.

sentences.zh: 文舉以選與諸公子游，雅相欽敬，未嘗戲狎。

translations.literal: Wenju through selection associated with the various young lords; they mutually esteemed each other with refinement and he never frolicked or treated them lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju was chosen to keep company with the princes; they held one another in refined esteem, and he never treated them lightly or familiarly.

sentences.zh: 遷威烈將軍、著作郎、中外府參軍事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to awe-inspiring general, compiler in the imperial library, and staff officer for inner and outer headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general who inspires awe, compiler in the imperial library, and staff officer for inner and outer headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，賜姓賀蘭氏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was granted the surname Helan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 of Emperor Gong of Wei he was granted the surname Helan.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，襲爵澄城縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he inherited the rank of Viscount of Chengcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Wenju inherited the rank of viscount of Chengcheng county.

sentences.zh: 齊公憲初開幕府，以文舉為司錄。

translations.literal: When Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian first opened his headquarters, he made Wenju registrar.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian first opened his headquarters, he appointed Wenju registrar.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，累遷帥都督、寧遠將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, through successive promotions he reached command leader, general who pacifies the distance, and grand area commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Shizong's reign he rose through command leader and general who pacifies the distance to grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 及憲出鎮劍南，復以文舉為益州總管府中郎。

translations.literal: When Xian went out to garrison Jiannan, Wenju was again made middle-rank officer in the Yi Province overall headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Xian went out to garrison Jiannan, Wenju was again made middle-rank officer in the Yi Province overall headquarters.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，就加使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng he received the added ranks of bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal in protocol to the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 2 he received the added ranks of bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 蜀土沃饒，商販百倍。

translations.literal: Shu territory was fertile and rich; merchant profits were tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was fertile and rich, and merchant profits there ran ten times higher.

sentences.zh: 或有勸文舉以利者，文舉答之曰：「利之為貴，莫若安身。

translations.literal: Some who urged Wenju toward profit — Wenju replied, saying: "Among things that are precious, none surpasses keeping oneself secure.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged Wenju to seek profit, he replied, "Of all things worth having, none surpasses keeping oneself secure.

sentences.zh: 身安則道隆，非貨之謂。

translations.literal: If the person is secure, then the Way is exalted — that is not what is meant by goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the person is secure, the Way is exalted — that is not what wealth means.

sentences.zh: 是以不為，非惡財也。

translations.literal: Therefore I do not act on it — not because I hate wealth.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I refuse — not because I hate wealth.

sentences.zh: 」憲矜其貧窶，每欲資給之。

translations.literal: " Xian pitied his poverty and always wished to supply and aid him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Xian pitied his poverty and always wished to supply him.

sentences.zh: 文舉恆自謙遜，辭多受少。

translations.literal: Wenju constantly was self-effacing; he declined much and accepted little.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju was always self-effacing, declining much and accepting little.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，遷絳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding he was transferred to Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 3 he was transferred to inspector of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 邃之往正平也，以廉約自守，每行春省俗，單車而已。

translations.literal: When Sui went to Zhengping, he kept himself through frugality and restraint; whenever he made spring rounds to inspect local custom, it was with a single carriage alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui went to Zhengping he lived frugally; whenever he made spring rounds to inspect local custom he traveled with a single carriage alone.

sentences.zh: 及文舉臨州，一遵其法。

translations.literal: When Wenju came to the prefecture, he wholly followed his father's methods.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenju took the province he followed his father's methods in every respect.

sentences.zh: 百姓美而化之。

translations.literal: The common people praised this and were transformed by it.
translations.idiomatic: The people praised this and were transformed by it.

sentences.zh: 總管韋孝寬特相欽重，每與談論，不覺膝前于席。

translations.literal: Overall commander Wei Xiaokuan especially esteemed and honored him; whenever they conversed, he unawares moved his knees forward on the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Overall commander Wei Xiaokuan especially esteemed him; whenever they talked, he unawares leaned forward on the mat.

sentences.zh: 天和初，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he was promoted to grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal in protocol to the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianhe he was promoted to grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 尋為孝寬柱國府司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was made marshal in Wei Xiaokuan's pillar headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed marshal in Wei Xiaokuan's pillar headquarters.

sentences.zh: 六年，入為司憲中大夫，進爵為公，增邑通前一千戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he entered court as grand master in the Censorate, advanced in enfeoffment to duke, with fief including prior grants reaching one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he entered court as grand master in the Censorate, was raised to duke, and his fief, old and new together, reached one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 俄轉軍司馬。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he was reassigned as army marshal.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，又增邑七百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande, fief was again increased by seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year 2 his fief was again increased by seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 文舉少喪父，其兄又在山東，唯與弟璣幼相訓養，友愛甚篤。

translations.literal: Wenju lost his father young; his elder brother was also in Shandong; he and his younger brother Ji alone from youth mutually instructed and reared each other, with very deep fraternal affection.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju lost his father young, and with his elder brother in Shandong he and his younger brother Ji alone reared and instructed one another from childhood in deep fraternal affection.

sentences.zh: 璣又早亡，文舉撫視遺孤，逾于己子。

translations.literal: Ji also died early; Wenju nurtured and cared for his orphaned children more than for his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji also died young, Wenju cared for his orphaned children even more devotedly than for his own sons.

sentences.zh: 時人以此稱之。

translations.literal: Men of the time for this reason praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 初，文舉叔父季和為曲沃令，卒于聞喜川，而叔母韋氏卒于正平縣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenju's paternal uncle Jihe was magistrate of Quwo; he died at Wenxi River, while his uncle's wife, Lady Wei, died in Zhengping county.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wenju's uncle Jihe, magistrate of Quwo, had died on the Wenxi River, while his aunt Lady Wei had died in Zhengping county.

sentences.zh: 屬東西分隔，韋氏墳壟在齊境。

translations.literal: Because east and west were divided, Lady Wei's tomb mound was in Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm was split between east and west, Lady Wei's grave lay in Qi territory.

sentences.zh: 及文舉在本州，每加賞募。

translations.literal: When Wenju was in his province, he repeatedly added rewards and recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: While Pei Wenju held his province, he repeatedly offered rewards to recruit help.

sentences.zh: 齊人感其孝義，潛相要結，以韋氏柩西歸，竟得合葬。

translations.literal: The people of Qi, moved by his filial piety and righteousness, secretly made mutual arrangements, and brought Lady Wei's coffin west; in the end husband and wife were buried together.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his filial devotion and righteousness, men of Qi secretly acted together to bring Lady Wei's coffin west, and husband and wife were at last buried together.

sentences.zh: 六年，除南青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Inspector of Southern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made inspector of Southern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanzheng year 1 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 子冑嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 官至大都督，早卒。

translations.literal: He reached the rank of grand area commander and died young.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand area commander but died young.

sentences.zh: 時有高賓者，歷官內外，亦以幹用見稱。

translations.literal: At the time there was Gao Bin, who through successive offices at court and in the regions was also praised for practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Gao Bin, who served in posts at court and in the provinces and was likewise praised for practical talent.

sentences.zh: 賓，渤海修人也。

translations.literal: Bin was a man of Xiuren in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bin came from Xiuren in Bohai commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先因官北邊，遂沒于遼左。

translations.literal: His ancestors, because of office on the northern frontier, thus ended up in the Liao region.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had gone north on government service and ended up in the Liao region.

sentences.zh: 祖暠，以魏太和初，自遼東歸魏。

translations.literal: Grandfather Hao, in the early Taihe era of Wei, returned to Wei from Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hao, in the early Taihe reign of Wei, came back from Liaodong to Wei.

sentences.zh: 官至安定郡守、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He reached the posts of Administrator of Anding commandery and Minister Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administrator of Anding commandery and minister steward.

sentences.zh: 父季安，撫軍將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ji'an was General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji'an held the ranks of general who pacifies the army and inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 賓少聰穎，有文武幹用。

translations.literal: Bin from youth was clever and keen; he had both civil and military practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Gao Bin was quick and sharp and showed practical talent in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 仕東魏，歷官至龍驤將軍、諫議大夫、立義都督。

translations.literal: He served Eastern Wei, rising through successive offices to General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Advisor for Remonstrance, and Commander Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Eastern Wei he rose through the ranks to general of agile cavalry, remonstrance advisor, and commander who establishes righteousness.

sentences.zh: 同列有忌其能者，譖之于齊神武。

translations.literal: Among colleagues there were those who envied his ability; they slandered him before Qi Divine Warrior.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues who envied his talent slandered him to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 賓懼及於難，大統六年，乃棄家屬，間行歸闕。

translations.literal: Bin feared that disaster would reach him; in the sixth year of Datong he abandoned his family members and by secret route returned to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, Gao Bin in Datong year 6 left his family behind and slipped back to the Zhou court by secret route.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，授安東將軍、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended this and appointed him General Who Pacifies the East and Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised this and made him general who pacifies the east and silver-gleam grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 稍遷通直散騎常侍、撫軍將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: Gradually he was transferred to Direct-Duty Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Grand Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to direct-duty regular attendant, general who pacifies the army, and grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除咸陽郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was appointed Administrator of Xianyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Shizong's reign he was made administrator of Xianyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 政存簡惠，甚得民和。

translations.literal: His government preserved simplicity and kindness, greatly winning the people's accord.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was simple and generous and won the people's full confidence.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞其能，賜田園於郡境。

translations.literal: Shizong heard of his ability and granted fields and gardens within the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong heard of his skill and granted him fields and gardens within the commandery.

sentences.zh: 賓旣羈旅歸國，親屬在齊，常慮見疑，無以取信。

translations.literal: Bin, having returned as an exile to the state, with kin in Qi, constantly feared being suspected and had no way to gain trust.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bin had come back as a refugee from abroad, with relatives still in Qi, and always feared suspicion with no way to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 乃於所賜田內，多蒔竹木，盛構堂宇，幷鑿池沼以環之，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Thereupon within the granted fields he planted many bamboo and trees, built halls and chambers on a grand scale, and also dug ponds and moats to ring them around, having the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: So on the granted land he planted bamboo and trees in abundance, built fine halls and chambers, and dug ponds around them, showing that he meant to settle there for life.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以此知無貳焉。

translations.literal: The court thereby knew he was not disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: The court took this as proof that he had no second loyalty.

sentences.zh: 加使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍，賜姓獨孤氏。

translations.literal: He was given the added ranks Bearer of the Staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies, and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, and granted the surname Dugu.
translations.idiomatic: He received the added ranks of bearer of the staff, general of chariots and cavalry, equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, and regular attendant of the scattered riders, and was granted the surname Dugu.

sentences.zh: 又有安定尞允，本姓牛氏，亦有器幹，知名於時。

translations.literal: There was also Liao Yun of Anding; his original surname was the Niu clan; he too had talent and practical ability and was renowned in his day.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Yun of Anding, originally surnamed Niu, who likewise had talent and force of character and was well known in his time.

sentences.zh: 歷官侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、工部尚書、臨涇縣公，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He held successive offices as Attendant Within, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Opening-Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies, Grand Master of the Ministry of Works, and Duke of Linjing county, and was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, grand master of the Ministry of Works, and duke of Linjing county, and was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 失其事，故不為傳。

translations.literal: His affairs were lost, so no biography was written.
translations.idiomatic: His deeds were lost, and no full biography was written.

sentences.zh: 允子弘，博學洽聞。

translations.literal: Yun's son Hong was broadly learned and widely informed.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's son Hong was learned and widely read.

sentences.zh: 宣政中，內史下大夫、儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: During Xuanzheng, he was lower grand master in the Inner History and equal-in-protocol grand general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanzheng era he was lower grand master in the Inner History and equal-in-protocol grand general.

sentences.zh: 大象末，復姓牛氏。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he restored the surname Niu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daxiang era he restored the surname Niu.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：寇儁委質兩朝，以儒素見重。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Kou Jun submitted his service to two dynasties and was honored for plain Confucian virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Kou Jun gave loyal service to two dynasties and was esteemed for simple Confucian integrity.

sentences.zh: 韓褒奉事三帝，以忠厚知名。

translations.literal: Han Bao served three emperors and was known for loyal kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Han Bao served three sovereigns and won fame for steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 趙肅平允當官。

translations.literal: Zhao Su was fair and even-handed in office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Su was even-handed in office.

sentences.zh: 張軌循良播美。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui spread the reputation of a virtuous administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui left a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 李彥譽流省閤。

translations.literal: Li Yan's fame flowed through the secretariat halls.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan's reputation filled the halls of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 郭彥信著蠻陬。

translations.literal: Guo Yan's trust was established among the barbarian frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yan won trust on the barbarian frontier.

sentences.zh: 歷官外內，竝當時之選也。

translations.literal: Serving in offices internal and external, all were choice men of their day.
translations.idiomatic: In posts at court and in the provinces, all were men chosen for excellence in their time.

sentences.zh: 文舉之在絳州，世載清德。

translations.literal: Wenju's time at Jiang Prefecture carried generations of pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wenju's tenure in Jiang Province continued a line of unstained virtue.

sentences.zh: 辭多受少，有廉讓之風焉。

translations.literal: Declining much and accepting little, he had the air of modest integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Declining much and accepting little, he showed the manners of frugal humility.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
